steps.name: Sample structure QC and count-table provenance check
caveats: The table's Salmon provenance is not established; the integrality check is the gate for treating it as raw counts - fractional (TPM / estimated-count-like) values would invalidate count-model fitting
Do not scale, transform, or normalize the counts before the model; any such transformation breaks the mean-variance relation the negative-binomial model expects
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-salmon-counts-unknown-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (gene-level output from Salmon as delivered; 12,000 genes x 12 samples plus a row-label column; the record does not state whether a length correction was applied) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-salmon-counts-unknown-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 samples, one condition column). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Per-sample Salmon quantification directories were not delivered.
steps.question: Do the 12 human skin samples (6 treated / atopic dermatitis lesional, 6 control) form two condition-coherent groups in expression space with no outlier sample, and is the delivered Salmon gene-level table usable as a raw count matrix?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

constraints: Do not run tximport: the table is already gene-level and no per-sample quantifications exist to import
If the integrality check fails (substantially fractional values), stop before any differential test and report that the delivered table is not a raw count matrix
steps.description: Verify the count matrix: values must be non-negative integers (report the fraction of non-integer entries; if the table is substantially fractional it is not a raw count matrix and a negative-binomial count model on it is invalid, in which case stop the pipeline and report that finding as the outcome of this run). Assert the condition column holds exactly the levels 'treated' and 'control' with 6 samples each, and that all 12 sample columns of counts.csv match the 12 metadata rows. Build the DESeq2 object, run the variance stabilizing transformation with blind=TRUE, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a heatmap of Euclidean distances between samples, all colored by condition.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample distance heatmap colored by condition (treated/control), with a written call on whether the samples form two condition-coherent groups and whether any sample departs from its group
The fraction of non-integer entries in counts.csv is reported and the table is confirmed to be non-negative integers (raw counts), or the pipeline stops with that finding as the run outcome
All 12 sample columns of counts.csv matched to the 12 metadata rows; condition column verified to contain exactly 6 'treated' and 6 'control' samples

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
steps.context: Uses the integer count matrix and the verified sample table from T1S1. 12,000 genes, 12 samples (6 treated / 6 control), unpaired, single batch, design ~ condition. Per-sample Salmon quantification files and an average transcript length table were not delivered, so no length offset can be applied; the counts are used as delivered.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) and control skin at FDR < 0.05, by the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca

steps.description: Pre-filter: drop genes with fewer than 10 counts in fewer than 6 samples (the smallest group size) and report how many were removed. Build the DESeqDataSet with design ~ condition and relevel so 'control' is the explicit reference. Fit DESeq: size factors are estimated by median-of-ratios inside the model, no pre-normalization of the counts. Extract results for the contrast c('condition', 'treated', 'control') with the Wald test, independent filtering on, and alpha = 0.05; then shrink the reported log2FoldChange with apeglm (the comparison is a single model coefficient, so apeglm rather than ashr). Plot the histogram of the unadjusted p-values and describe its shape. Report the number of genes tested after the filter, the number of DE genes at padj < 0.05, and count separately genes with NA p-values from the count-outlier flag (6 < 7 replicates per cell, so DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers) from genes removed by the independent filter. Export the full results table (baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, shrunken_log2FoldChange), the MA plot, and the dispersion plot.
acceptance_criteria: Full DESeq2 results table for all tested genes with baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and shrunken_log2FoldChange; contrast direction is treated vs control so positive log2FoldChange means higher in treated
Number of DE genes at padj < 0.05 reported, with genes carrying NA p-values from the count-outlier flag and genes removed by independent filtering reported separately
MA plot, dispersion plot, and unadjusted p-value histogram saved, with the histogram's shape described
The step output states that no length offset was applied because the per-sample Salmon quantification files and the average transcript length table were not delivered

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (second method for robustness)
caveats: Same lost-length-offset caveat as T1S2: the count table is Salmon gene-level output with no length offset applied, so changes in isoform use can masquerade as differential expression; state this in the step output
Do not reuse DESeq2's pre-filter or size factors here: TMM and filterByExpr are the edgeR path's own normalization and filtering
steps.context: Same verified integer count matrix and sample table as T1S2, from T1S1. 12,000 genes, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. No length offset is applied (per-sample Salmon quantifications and the average transcript length table were not delivered), the same data state as the DESeq2 step, so the two methods' gene sets are directly comparable.
steps.question: Does the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test recover the same differentially expressed gene set as DESeq2 for treated vs control, and how large is the intersection of the two methods' FDR < 0.05 sets?

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (M-0003) is the permitted second method per R-0001@9a17 for 2-11 replicates per group, run to supply the two-method overlap the report step requires (R-0042@54e1); 6 replicates per group is within range.

constraints: model_design: design ~ condition with 'control' as the reference level; contrast treated vs control
filter_low_counts: filterByExpr before the model (the edgeR-path replacement for DESeq2 independent filtering)
normalize: TMM scaling factors; no pre-normalization of the counts
multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment at alpha = 0.05; select by adjusted p-value only, never by unadjusted p-value or fold change alone
steps.description: Filter genes with filterByExpr before the model. Normalize with TMM scaling factors. Fit the GLM with design ~ condition ('control' the reference), estimate quasi-likelihood dispersion with glmQLFit, and test the treated vs control contrast with the quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFTest). Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha = 0.05 and select genes by FDR only. Export the results table (logFC, pvalue, FDR) and the DE gene list at FDR < 0.05, and compute the overlap with the T1S2 DE list: the number of genes called by both methods, the number called by DESeq2 only, and the number called by edgeR only.
acceptance_criteria: Full edgeR QL results table (logFC, pvalue, FDR) for the tested genes, with the treated vs control direction (positive logFC = higher in treated)
Number of DE genes at FDR < 0.05, plus the overlap with the T1S2 DE set: genes shared by both methods, DESeq2-only genes, and edgeR-only genes each reported by count and by gene list

steps.name: Report
steps.context: Combines the outputs of T1S2 (DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm-shrunken LFC, MA/dispersion/p-value-histogram diagnostics) and T1S4 (edgeR QL F-test with its DE list and the computed overlap). 12,000-gene input table, 6 treated vs 6 control human skin, single batch.
steps.question: What is the final differentially expressed gene list for treated vs control skin, which genes are high-confidence (both methods agree), and what must the report state about the unverified Salmon count table?
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
steps.description: Assemble the final report: (1) the DE gene table with baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken, from the test), shrunken_log2FoldChange (apeglm - name the shrinkage estimator in the header), lfcSE, pvalue, and padj, ranked by the shrunken log2FoldChange, keeping the p-values from the unshrunken fit; (2) the MA plot, the dispersion plot, and the unadjusted p-value histogram with its shape described, placed before the gene tables; (3) the DE gene counts per method, the intersection treated as the high-confidence set, and the genes called by only one method as secondary sets named after that method - never present the union as the result; (4) the number of genes tested after the filter and the number of DE genes at adjusted p-value < 0.05, with genes carrying NA p-values from the outlier flag and genes removed by independent filtering counted separately; (5) a statement that the count table is Salmon gene-level output as delivered, that per-sample quantification files and the average transcript length table were not delivered, that no length offset was applied, and that changes in isoform use can show as differential expression; (6) the report fields: method, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info; (7) if the row identifiers of counts.csv are not gene symbols, map them to HGNC symbols using the human gene annotation available in the environment and keep both identifier columns, otherwise report with the identifiers as delivered. Set and record a fixed random seed, and store the reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package versions, annotation release) with the results.
acceptance_criteria: Final DE gene table ranked by shrunken log2FoldChange, retaining the unshrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header
MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram appear before the gene tables, with the histogram's shape described
High-confidence intersection set and the per-method secondary sets are reported, and the union is not presented as the result
Report states method, package versions, design, contrast, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info, the seed, and the lost-length-offset caveat

plan.title: Atopic dermatitis skin DE: DESeq2 and edgeR
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered one gene-level count table (12,000 genes x 12 samples) from Salmon for human skin, 6 treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, with no per-sample quantifications and no record of whether the length correction was applied, so the table's provenance is not established. The plan first validates that the delivered table is a raw count matrix (non-negative integers) and inspects sample structure (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, distance heatmap) to confirm the samples separate by condition with no outlier before any test runs. The primary test is the DESeq2 Wald test with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, an explicit control reference, apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, and independent filtering with Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05. Because no per-sample Salmon quantification files or average transcript length table were delivered, no length offset is applied: the model is fitted on the counts as delivered, and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that changes in isoform use can masquerade as differential expression. The edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test, the permitted second method for 2-11 replicates per group, runs in parallel on the identical data so the report can carry the two-method overlap; the intersection is the high-confidence set and method-only genes are secondary sets, never the union. The report ranks genes by the shrunken log2 fold change, includes MA, dispersion, and p-value-histogram diagnostics, and names method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_DE, and session info.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
